This word has three distinct meanings depending on context. Each one is completely different from the others, so knowing all three is essential.
Meaning 1: A physical connection to a system

This is the most literal meaning. A hookup is a point where something — a machine, a vehicle, an appliance — gets connected to a supply line such as electricity, water, gas, or a cable network.

Think of it like a plug socket, but for bigger systems.

Examples:

  • An RV (a large motorhome) at a campsite needs a water hookup and an electrical hookup to get running water and power.
  • "The new washing machine needs a proper hookup to the plumbing before it works."
  • "Does your apartment have a cable hookup?"

This meaning is neutral, technical, and perfectly everyday. You'll hear it from plumbers, electricians, campers, and people setting up appliances.
Meaning 2: A casual sexual encounter — or the person involved in it

This is the most culturally prominent meaning today, especially in American English. A hookup refers to a casual sexual encounter between two people — one where there is no romantic commitment, no ongoing relationship, and usually no expectation that things will continue afterward.

The key qualities of a hookup in this sense:

  • Casual: not part of a serious relationship
  • Short-term: often a one-time thing, or at least not regular
  • No strings attached: neither person owes the other a relationship, date, or even a follow-up conversation

Crucially, "hookup" is intentionally vague about the specific physical acts involved. It's a deliberately flexible word that can refer to anything from kissing to sexual intercourse. People use this vagueness on purpose — it lets them acknowledge that something happened without spelling out the details. So if someone says "we had a hookup," it tells you there was a sexual or physical encounter, but not exactly what kind.

The word can also refer to the person you had that encounter with:

  • "She was just a hookup" means she was someone he had a casual sexual encounter with, not a girlfriend.
  • "He's my hookup" could mean a person he occasionally has casual sex with (though context matters — see Meaning 3).

Who uses this word: It's most common among younger adults (roughly teens to thirties), in university/college settings, and in the context of dating apps. It's informal and conversational, not used in formal writing.

Register: Informal slang. Not offensive, but not polite company language either. Completely normal in casual conversation.
Meaning 3: A contact who can get you something — or the thing they provide

A hookup can also refer to a person who has access to something that is hard to get, and who can get it for you. It's like a "connection" or "contact" in a back-channel sense.

You use it this way: "I have a hookup for…" or "Do you have a hookup?"

Examples:

  • "I got a hookup for cheap concert tickets" — meaning he knows someone who can get him tickets at a lower price or bypassing normal channels.
  • "Do you have a hookup for good sneakers?" — Do you know someone who can get me good sneakers, maybe at a discount or before they sell out?
  • In drug culture specifically, "my hookup" very commonly refers to one's drug dealer or supplier. This is one of the most established uses of the word in this sense.

This meaning is about access through a person, rather than a physical or romantic connection.
How to tell which meaning is intended

Context does all the work:

If someone talks about…The meaning is likely…
Appliances, camping, wiring, plumbingPhysical connection (Meaning 1)
Two people, last night, a date, a partyCasual sexual encounter (Meaning 2)
Getting something — tickets, products, substancesA supplier/contact (Meaning 3)

The word "hookup" comes from the verb "to hook up," and all three noun meanings flow naturally from that verb — connecting a wire, connecting physically with a person, or connecting with a supplier. So if you already understand "hook up" as a verb in any of those senses, the noun simply names the result or the person involved in that act.
